g.text: Section through one rib, square to the slope, 1:10

svg.text: Roof grid B: diamond lattice
one roof face seen square on
(1) Diagonals parallel to the two hips (same inclination as the
roof edges, 59.0° in the face), every 1250 along the base: equal
diamonds 1250 wide.
(2) Bottom ring = the 300 solid base; top ring at the crown. The
hips are two of the diagonals. No other horizontal ribs.
(3*) Rib (column): printed channel 160 wide x 240 deep in the 160
air zone + layer 2, filled with cast concrete, 4 Ø16 + Ø8 stirrups
every 200 (assumed).
(4) Inner layer 1, 80: continuous, covers the grid on the room
side.
(5) Outer skin 80: continuous, covers the grid on the outside
(cladding on it).
(6*) Between the ribs the air zone stays open for thermal
insulation (dotted).
* = assumed, to confirm
Notes
Every diagonal ends on a ring or on a hip, so no bar has a
free end in the shell.
Diagonals do not stop as the roof narrows: the diamonds
just get clipped by the hips.
Rough quantities, four faces (hips counted twice, so
slightly high): ribs 318 m, 4 Ø16 each bars, steel 2006
kg, cast concrete 12.2 m3.
Rib size, bar count and the 160 x 240 channel are
assumptions for the engineer to check. Elevation shows the
face square on; true lengths are 1.25 x the drawn heights.
m
